checklist: THE HAND COMES DOWN AND ESTABLISHES THE POST

YES, later than the reference. The arm reaches DOWN to beside / behind the hip with a bent elbow and the hand lands at +0.24 / 0.36 / 0.45 s (SP2F +0.10 / 0.22 / 0.28 s; REFERENCE3 ≈ at the hip landing).
THE HAND STAYS LOW / ON THE TURF
YES. Continuous turf contact from first contact to the end of the slide at all speeds — no gaps (also none in 30 perturbed runs).
THE HAND SLIDES WITH THE PLAYER (the relatively stable end of the chain)

YES. Its drift relative to the pelvis over the contact is 0.23 / 0.29 / 0.24 m (SP2F 0.76 / 1.01 / 0.93 m, SP2F2 0.68 / 0.76 / 0.86 m), and it stays OUTBOARD of the posting shoulder throughout (≥ 0.27 / 0.39 / 0.41 m) — in SP2F / SP2F2 the shoulder ends up outside the hand (-0.10 / -0.22 / -0.31 m) as the hand is dragged back.
THE ARM ANGLE CHANGES BECAUSE THE TORSO LOWERS RELATIVE TO THE HAND

YES. The shoulder descends toward the hand (hand − shoulder height -0.62 → -0.21 / -0.62 → -0.29 / -0.60 → -0.36 m) while the upper arm keeps pointing DOWN (-78…-40 / -68…-44 / -54…-43°); in SP2F / SP2F2 the upper arm rises to -22 / -18 / -4° (≈ horizontal) as the long arm is swept back along the turf.
THE ELBOW FLEXES / EXTENDS COMPLIANTLY (not a straight spoke)
YES. Elbow 45 → 114 / 17 → 67 / 8 → 40°, progressive, as weight comes on; SP2F2: -7…-2 / -6…10 / -7…23° (straight).
NO GIANT OVERHEAD SWEEP OF THE POSTING ARM

YES for the posting arm (it stays low and behind / beside the torso; no authored arm angles after contact). Note: the tall raised arm in all of these views is the TACKLING-SIDE arm, which SP2D–SP2F2 deliberately move up / over the body (REFERENCE3's other arm is raised too). It is unchanged here so the posting-arm correction can be judged alone; it can be lowered next.
TORSO RECLINES GRADUALLY · NO SUDDEN FALL

YES. Peak trunk rate after landing 116 / 125 / 157°/s (SP2F 98 / 107 / 143), backward rock ≤ 2.9°, never chest-down, no failure / fallback. The trunk still sits upright ≈ 0.4 s after landing (as in SP2F): the lean onto the arm starts once the hand is down.
REMOVED. Folded-knee tibial rotation past its stop 1.9 / 1.0 / 1.7° (SP2F 1.7 / 1.0 / 1.5°, SP2F2 7.6 / 6.4 / 5.1°): no counter-lean is released in the air.
Run-to-tackle transition, dive / scissor, folded-leg tuck, boot, root / COM, body, recipient and C3 unchanged; F37.5 unchanged (temporary); no friction calibration, no recipient work.
reviewNote: I cannot play video in real time. I reviewed the focused side-by-side frame by frame at 30 fps (every frame of the 1× clip at 30 fps), plus the side and torso-only views and the traces.
diagnosis: SP2F / SP2F2: after contact the posting hand is NOT the stable end of the chain. The turf drags it backward and outward relative to the pelvis by 0.68 / 0.76 / 0.86 m (SP2F2) while the elbow stays straight (-7…-2 / -6…10 / -7…23°) and the upper arm rises from pointing down to ≈ horizontal: a long straight lever swept back along the turf. The 120–135° "shoulder angle" was that sweep, not the torso lowering onto a planted hand.
The tall raised arm in the SP2F / SP2F2 rear and side views is the tackling-side arm (up / over the body since SP2D), not the posting arm.
reference: REFERENCE3, 20 hand-annotated frames (evidence/REFERENCE3_arm_annotation.json): its player slides on his RIGHT side (we see his back; the posting arm is his right). His posting hand stays at a near-constant image offset beside / slightly behind the hip from the landing on; the shoulder descends toward the hand's height; the elbow bends progressively (≈ 9° → 79° in the image); the upper arm stays steep (≈ −65 … −87°) while the forearm flattens onto the turf (≈ −78° → −8°): a forearm post that the torso lowers onto.
changes: The post built FROM THE HAND OUTWARD (new opt-in sp2_ctrl post.hold): at the first forearm contact the hand's horizontal offset from the pelvis is captured (translation only — the body may turn about it) and a compliant, capped spring-damper (600 N/m, 60 N·s/m, ≤ 120 N) keeps the hand there, so it slides with the player instead of being dragged toward the head. Its height is left to the turf contact and a light 60 N press.

The arm as an ECCENTRIC SUPPORT STRUT: an axial push (60 N) plus a damper on the shoulder's closing speed toward the hand (1600 N·s/m, ≤ 1000 N, only while the arm points upward from the hand) — it resists being compressed quickly (it manages the fall) but shortens as the torso lowers, and it does not resist the arm rotating about the hand. The elbow keeps 30 % of its stiffness toward its angle AT CONTACT (it yields progressively instead of locking straight and buckling); the shoulder has no angle target.
Reach: the hand goes DOWN beside / behind the hip with the elbow bent (abduction 45°, extension 35°, elbow 35°, by 0.62 s).

Torso: SP2F's (no in-air counter-lean release — so no folded-knee overrun) plus a gradual lean onto the planted arm after contact (lumbar −5°, thoracic −14° over 0.62 → 1.52 s); pelvis-roll objective 60° (75° rolled the trunk over the arm, onto it).

New: the hand-relative diagnostic (hand − pelvis, hand − shoulder, hand height, elbow, upper-arm / forearm orientation, shoulder / elbow angular velocity, hand speed, image-plane projection) and the REFERENCE3 annotation.
notes: The hand plants later than in SP2F (+0.24 / 0.36 / 0.45 s): from an upright trunk a bent-elbow reach meets the turf only as the trunk starts to lean. A straighter reach plants earlier but locks the elbow straight and buckles it at 4.5 m/s (log §4).
The corrected forearm ends pointing back / down beside the hip (toward the camera) rather than straight out to the side as in REFERENCE3.
The upright seated phase after the landing (≈ 0.4 s, SP2F's) remains; the lateral lean onto the arm starts after the hand is down.
At 4.5 m/s the elbow ends at ≈ 114° (forearm flat on the turf, body low).
Sustained small excursions: posting shoulder_L.x ≈ 2° at 4.5 m/s; hip_L.x ≈ 1.5° (both ≤ SP2F-era levels except the shoulder, which is new: the strut loads the shoulder).
The image-plane comparison is qualitative: monocular, hand-annotated (±5 px), different camera and character proportions; it is mirrored so that the posting side is + in both.
